- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.75) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially after spikes.
- If model shows sharp upward trend after a recent spike, it often overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak or adjust downward 1–3 days later.
- When sentiment is low (≤0.3) and price is falling, model often underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term sentiment shifts; apply smoothing filter (e.g., 3-day moving average) to forecast if sentiment volatility > 0.25.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion after a strong move, model often fails to correct; adjust forecast to align with 3–5-day moving average of history.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate early in the period; reduce first 5–7 days’ forecast by 0.5–1.5% if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If sentiment is high but price drops sharply, model often fails to anticipate; add 1–2% downward correction to forecast if sentiment > 0.75 and price drops > 1.5% from peak.
